from.author: agent
from.tooltip: Drawn as pass-through, because that is how it was described. **No failure exit is drawn** — see the pinned question on the sanctions screen; the same gap applies here.

to.author: agent
to.tooltip: A failed identity check is a **hard stop** — straight to the rejection log, never onward to banding. Confirmed with the desk 2026-08-27.

from.author: agent
from.tooltip:
Drawn as pass-through: everything reaching it continues to risk banding.

**This is almost certainly incomplete.** A sanctions hit normally stops a request where it stands rather than banding it. Pinned.

to.author: agent
to.tooltip:
A hit is a **hard stop** — straight to the rejection log and a letter, never onward to banding. Confirmed with the desk 2026-08-27.

The first draft drew this as pass-through, which would have let a sanctioned party reach the banding step.

from.author: agent
from.tooltip:
Sweeps once a day. Anything sitting in manual review more than two days is pushed back to banding.

Drawn as a loop back into banding, which is what was described — note that means a request can be re-banded repeatedly. Pinned.

to.author: agent
to.tooltip:
Sweeps once a day. A case stuck in manual review more than two days goes back to banding — **but only twice**. Anything swept twice is escalated to a human on the third pass rather than re-banded.

That limit is a real rule, confirmed 2026-08-27, not a drawing convenience.

from.author: agent
from.tooltip:
A human looks at the case.

Deliberately **not** called a review queue: Argus already has a *Review queue* for sub-threshold Signals and the two are unrelated. Same word, different system.

Only one exit is drawn — approved. Whether a reviewer can also refuse is pinned.

to.author: agent
to.tooltip:
A human looks at the case. **Three ways out**: approve to account opening, refuse to the rejection log, or sit long enough to be swept.

Deliberately not called a review queue: Argus already has a *Review queue* for sub-threshold Signals and the two are unrelated systems.

from.author: agent
from.tooltip:
**The audit trail for a refusal.** Distinct from the letter on purpose: the log is the record that survives, the letter is what the client receives.

Compliance will ask what is retained here and for how long. Nothing in this drawing answers that.

to.author: agent
to.tooltip:
**Four ways in, and everything that dies lands here**: a failed identity check, a sanctions hit, a refusal at banding, and a reviewer's refusal.

Confirmed with the desk 2026-08-27. The first two are hard stops — they never reach banding at all.

This is the audit trail; the letter is what the client receives. Compliance will ask what is retained here and for how long, and nothing in this drawing answers that.

registry_changes.reason: one landscape page for the compliance pack: three intake routes, the linear checks, a three-way band, four failure routes converging on the rejection log, the four-eyes funding control and the bounded sweep. The failure fan is the part compliance cares about most and must not be on a second sheet.

summary.headline: rewired Account opening→Funding to Account opening→Second sign-off (+29 more)

user_note: desk answers: identity fail, sanctions hit, banding refuse and reviewer refuse all land in the rejection log — four ways in. Sweep escalates on the third pass instead of re-banding. Second sign-off added between account opening and funding.
